title: 1994 AHSME Problem 17
statement: An \(8\) by \(2\sqrt2\) rectangle has the same center as a circle of radius \(2.\) The area of the region common to both the rectangle and the circle is

solutions.text: The rectangle is wider than the circle, so the common region is the circle with the top and bottom caps beyond distance \(\sqrt2\) from the center removed. One cap has area \[ \begin{aligned} 2^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) &-\sqrt2\sqrt{2^2-(\sqrt2)^2}\\ &=\pi-2. \end{aligned} \] Therefore the common area is \(4\pi-2(\pi-2)=2\pi+4.\) Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: The rectangle removes two congruent caps from the circle
The cap chord is at distance \(\sqrt2\) from the center, so its half central angle is \(45^\circ\)
